n7-licao-scheduler.titulo: The real-estate agent picks the building
n7-licao-scheduler.enunciado:
Every new pod goes through the scheduler, in two steps:

  1. Filter: crosses out the nodes that won’t do (closed off, with a taint the pod doesn’t tolerate, missing the requested label, short on CPU or memory, affinity and spread rules).
  2. Score: among the ones left, prefers the one that meets the preferences, spreads the replicas and is the least busy.

If no node passes the filter, the pod stays Pending, and the reason is in the events:

0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s),
2 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector.

Read it like this: 3 buildings, none of them worked; 1 had a restriction sign (the control plane), 2 didn’t have the requested label.

Choosing where to live

  • nodeSelector: “only in a building with these labels”. Simple and mandatory.
  • affinity.nodeAffinity: the same, with more features (In, NotIn, Exists) and in two strengths: required (mandatory: with no node that meets it, Pending) or preferred (if possible).
  • affinity.podAntiAffinity: away from certain pods (the two backup copies in different buildings); podAffinity: close to them. The topologyKey says what “close” means: the same node (kubernetes.io/hostname) or the same zone (topology.kubernetes.io/zone).
  • topologySpreadConstraints: spread a group across nodes or zones, with a maximum difference (maxSkew) between the fullest and the emptiest.

Restricted building: taints and tolerations

A taint is a sign on the node that repels pods (kubectl taint nodes node-2 dedicado=gpu:NoSchedule). A toleration on the pod says “I’m allowed in”. Effects: NoSchedule (no new pod gets in), PreferNoSchedule (avoid it, if possible) and NoExecute (and also evicts whoever is already there).

The gotcha: a toleration allows, it doesn’t require. To send the pod to the restricted building, combine the toleration with a nodeSelector (or affinity). The kind control plane has a taint: that’s why your pods never go there.
n7-licao-scheduler.vidaReal: The real-estate agent (the scheduler) gets each new apartment, crosses out the buildings that won’t do and, among the ones left, picks the best.
n7-licao-scheduler.limite: The agent only picks on arrival: a pod never changes nodes on its own. If the node goes bad later, all that happens is a new pod being created (and only if there’s a Deployment).

n7-gerador.enunciado:
In the condo, only node-2 has a generator: it has the label energia=gerador (check with kubectl get nodes --show-labels).

Make the 2 replicas of caixa (the cash register) run only in the building with the generator.
n7-gerador.vidaReal: The store wants the cash register in a building with a generator: if the power goes out, sales keep going.
n7-gerador.limite: nodeSelector is mandatory: if the generator building fills up or is closed off, the new caixa waits at the door (Pending).
n7-gerador.comoSaber: kubectl get pods -o wide: the NODE column shows node-2 for both.

testes.descricao: both caixa replicas in the generator building

n7-etiqueta-no-predio.enunciado: The busca (search) pod is Pending. Find the reason (kubectl describe pod NAME, in the Events) and, from the terminal, put the label it asks for on node-1.
n7-etiqueta-no-predio.vidaReal: The search engine only accepts a building with a fast disk. node-1 has an SSD, but nobody put the label on the door.
n7-etiqueta-no-predio.limite: A label is just a label: Kubernetes doesn’t check whether the node really has an SSD. A wrong label sends the pod to the wrong place.
n7-etiqueta-no-predio.comoSaber: Within a few seconds the pod leaves Pending and goes to node-1.

n7-preferencia.enunciado:
node-2 (the one with the generator) is closed off for renovation, and vitrine (the showcase) is stuck Pending: its affinity is required (required...).

Switch it to a preferred affinity (preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution, weight 100): vitrine opens right away, in another building, and goes back to preferring the generator once it’s back up.
n7-preferencia.dica: preferred: [{ weight: 100, preference: { matchExpressions: [...] } }] (without the nodeSelectorTerms)
n7-preferencia.vidaReal: The showcase can open in any building; it just prefers the one with the generator. But the request said “only with a generator”, and that one is under renovation.
n7-preferencia.limite: A preference doesn’t move anyone afterwards: when the generator building comes back, vitrine stays where it is until the pods are replaced.
n7-preferencia.comoSaber: The 2 replicas become ready on node-1.

testes.descricao: vitrine opens even with the generator under renovation
the renovation ends and, on the next rollout, vitrine moves to the generator building

n7-backups-separados.enunciado:
backup has 2 replicas. Make sure two replicas are never on the same node, with a required anti-affinity between its pods (topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname).

If someone ever asks for more replicas than there are buildings, the extra one must wait (Pending), not share a building.
n7-backups-separados.dica: affinity.podAntiAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: [{ labelSelector: { matchLabels: { app: backup } }, topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname }]
n7-backups-separados.vidaReal: Keeping both backup copies in the same building is having just one copy: if the building catches fire, both are gone.
n7-backups-separados.limite: With the required rule, when buildings run short the extra copy waits (Pending). For “keep them apart if possible”, use preferred.
n7-backups-separados.comoSaber: kubectl get pods -o wide: each replica on its own node.

testes.descricao: with 3 replicas and 2 buildings, the third one waits

n7-zonas.enunciado:
The nodes have the topology.kubernetes.io/zone label: node-1 and node-2 in zona-a, node-3 in zona-b.

site has 6 replicas. Spread them across the zones, with a maximum difference of 1 (3 and 3), using topologySpreadConstraints.
n7-zonas.dica: topologySpreadConstraints: [{ maxSkew: 1, topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone, whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule, labelSelector: {...} }]
n7-zonas.vidaReal: The condo has two neighborhoods: A, with two buildings, and B, with one. If one neighborhood loses power, half the stores have to stay open.
n7-zonas.limite: Spreading by node isn’t spreading by zone: 2 per building leaves 4 in neighborhood A and only 2 in B.
n7-zonas.comoSaber: kubectl get pods -o wide: 3 replicas on node-3 and 3 split between node-1 and node-2.

n7-predio-restrito.enunciado:
node-2 has the GPU, the label dedicado=gpu and the taint dedicado=gpu:NoSchedule.

treino (training) already asks for the right building (nodeSelector), but it’s Pending. Give it the toleration for the building’s taint.
n7-predio-restrito.dica: tolerations: [{ key: dedicado, operator: Equal, value: gpu, effect: NoSchedule }]
n7-predio-restrito.vidaReal: The GPU building has a sign: “authorized personnel only”. The training job has the right address, but not the authorization.
n7-predio-restrito.limite: The authorization (toleration) doesn’t take anyone there: the nodeSelector does. With only the toleration, the pod can land in any building.
n7-predio-restrito.comoSaber: The treino pod becomes ready on node-2.

testes.descricao: treino runs in the GPU building
loja stays out of the restricted building

n7-tirar-a-placa.enunciado: impressao (printing) only runs on node-1 (that’s where the printer is), and its pod is Pending. Find out what’s blocking it (kubectl describe node node-1) and, from the terminal, take the sign down.
n7-tirar-a-placa.dica: kubectl taint nodes node-1 obra=sim:NoSchedule-  (the “-” at the end removes it)
n7-tirar-a-placa.vidaReal: The renovation on node-1 is over, but nobody took down the “under renovation” sign: the printer, which only exists there, was left unattended.
n7-tirar-a-placa.limite: Removing the NoSchedule taint doesn’t bring back whoever left: it only lets the next ones in.
n7-tirar-a-placa.comoSaber: kubectl describe node node-1 shows Taints: <none>, and the pod becomes ready.

testes.descricao: the sign is gone and printing is back

n7-licao-manutencao.titulo: Renovating the building: cordon, drain and PDB
n7-licao-manutencao.enunciado:
Swapping a disk, updating the system, rebooting the machine: every now and then a node needs maintenance.

  • kubectl cordon node-1: closes it off. No new pod gets in; whoever is there stays (STATUS Ready,SchedulingDisabled).
  • kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets: closes it off and empties it, evicting the pods one by one. Pods with an owner (Deployment, StatefulSet) are reborn on another node. drain refuses unless you allow it: --ignore-daemonsets (DaemonSet pods stay: one per node, on purpose), --delete-emptydir-data (the work desk is wiped) and --force (a pod with no owner doesn’t come back).
  • kubectl uncordon node-1: frees the node. Nobody comes back on their own: only the next pods can go there.

The PodDisruptionBudget

drain evicts through the eviction API, which respects PDBs: “from this group, at least 2 always ready” (minAvailable: 2) or “at most 1 out” (maxUnavailable: 1). With no slack, the eviction is refused and drain retries every 5 seconds, while the replacements come up on another node:

error when evicting pods/"loja-..." -n "default" (will retry after 5s):
Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod's disruption budget.

When the building goes down

If the kubelet stops (power, network, machine), the node turns NotReady in about 50 seconds and gets the node.kubernetes.io/unreachable taint. Its pods leave the Services and, 5 minutes later (the default 300 s toleration), they are evicted: the ones from a Deployment are reborn on another node; a standalone pod stays Terminating forever and doesn’t come back.

Priority

A PriorityClass gives an importance number (priorityClassName on the pod). With no room, the scheduler can remove lower-priority pods to make way for the more important one (preemption), like the ambulance that cuts to the front.
n7-licao-manutencao.vidaReal: To renovate a building, the management office closes off the entrance (cordon), moves the residents to other buildings (drain) and agrees beforehand on how many elevators must keep running (PDB).
n7-licao-manutencao.limite: The agreement (PDB) covers planned renovation. A power outage doesn’t ask permission: the building goes down with whoever is inside.

n7-interditar.enunciado: From the terminal, close off node-2 to new pods, without removing the ones already there.
n7-interditar.vidaReal: There’s renovation work on node-2 next week: starting today, no new resident moves in. Those who already live there stay.
n7-interditar.limite: Closing it off doesn’t empty it: the pods there stay until a drain (or until they die on their own).
n7-interditar.comoSaber: kubectl get nodes shows Ready,SchedulingDisabled on node-2, and loja still has 3 pods.

n7-esvaziar.enunciado: From the terminal, empty node-1 with kubectl drain (DaemonSet pods stay: use the right option). Then pretend you swapped the disk and hand the node back to the condo.
n7-esvaziar.dica: kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets and, afterwards, kubectl uncordon node-1
n7-esvaziar.vidaReal: node-1 is getting a new disk: move everyone to the other buildings, do the swap and hand the building back to the condo.
n7-esvaziar.limite: Handing the building back (uncordon) doesn’t bring the residents back: they stay where they are until someone replaces the pods.
n7-esvaziar.comoSaber: loja still has 3 ready pods, all on node-2, and node-1 is back to Ready.

n7-pdb.enunciado:
The 3 loja replicas are on node-1, which is going into maintenance. The PDB left in pdb.yaml should guarantee at least 2 ready during the drain, but it doesn’t protect anyone (check kubectl get pdb after applying).

Fix the PDB.
n7-pdb.dica: The PDB’s selector must match the labels of the loja pods (app: loja).
n7-pdb.vidaReal: Agreed with the management office: during the renovation, at least 2 of the store’s elevators keep running. But the agreement was written with the wrong name.
n7-pdb.limite: The PDB only applies to whoever evicts through the API (drain, node autoscaler). A kubectl delete or a node going down ignores it.
n7-pdb.comoSaber: kubectl get pdb shows ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS 1 (3 ready, 2 required).

testes.descricao: during the drain, the PDB holds the line and loja moves entirely to node-2

n7-prioridade.enunciado:
The nodes are full: 4 relatorios (reports) replicas ask for 900m of CPU each. pagamento (payments, 500m) is Pending due to Insufficient cpu.

In pagamento.yaml, create a PriorityClass critico (value 100000) and use it in pagamento. The scheduler will remove a report to free up the spot.
n7-prioridade.dica: Two documents in the file (separated by ---): the PriorityClass (apiVersion scheduling.k8s.io/v1, value: 100000) and the Deployment with priorityClassName: critico.
n7-prioridade.vidaReal: The condo is packed with reports, and payments just arrived: without them, the store can’t sell. The ambulance goes first and tows the parked car out of the spot.
n7-prioridade.limite: Whoever is removed really leaves: the evicted report goes back to the queue (Pending) and only runs when there’s room to spare.
n7-prioridade.comoSaber: pagamento becomes ready, and one report turns Pending (in its Events: Preempted).

msgs.2: a report was removed to free up the spot

n7-predio-caiu.enunciado: node-2 went down. Look at the nodes and the pods (-o wide) and answer: which pod won’t come back on its own?
n7-predio-caiu.dica: kubectl get nodes and kubectl get pods -o wide: who is Terminating on node-2 and has no replacement?
n7-predio-caiu.vidaReal: node-2 lost power a few minutes ago. The store has already reopened in another building; someone was left behind.
n7-predio-caiu.limite: Kubernetes doesn’t know whether the building went down or just lost its phone: that’s why it waits 5 minutes and leaves the pods “Terminating” until it hears back.

testes.descricao: you found who was left behind
